general_information.Syllabus Name: Media Planning _ Lập kế hoạch truyền thông
general_information.Description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of modern media planning practices, with a strong emphasis on the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in strategic media decision-making. Students will learn the complete process of designing, implementing, and optimizing media plans that align with brand communication objectives. Key topics include media selection, media mix strategy, audience segmentation, scheduling, performance metrics, and budgeting. The course highlights the practical role of AI in supporting media strategy. Students will apply AI-based tools in hands-on class projects to enhance their analytical and planning skills. By the end of the course, students will have developed practical media planning competencies and critical thinking abilities to address real-world communication challenges.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of modern media planning practices, with a strong emphasis on the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in strategic media decision-making. Students will learn the complete process of designing, implementing, and optimizing media plans that align with brand communication objectives. Key topics include media selection, media mix strategy, audience segmentation, scheduling, performance metrics, and budgeting. The course highlights the practical role of AI in supporting media strategy. Students will apply AI-based tools in hands-on class projects to enhance their analytical and planning skills. By the end of the course, students will have developed practical media planning competencies and critical thinking abilities to address real-world communication challenges.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify the role and functions of media planning within marketing, advertising, and communication environments.
Analyze media costs, scheduling, and audience measurement to design effective media strategies.
Evaluate competitive, cultural, and ethical challenges faced by media planners in a dynamic communication environment.
Develop professional-standard media plans that integrate diverse media channels and audience insights.
Collaborate in teams to design, present, and defend media plans that address real-world communication challenges.
Apply tools, software, and artificial intelligence (AI) to analyze media data and optimize planning decisions.

assessments.Question Type: Each student will analyze a real-world communication or advertising campaign to understand its strategic components, media execution, and overall effectiveness. The report should be 1,800 words minimum and focus on a current campaign that utilizes multiple media platforms. Tasks: Identify and classify the product/service and its direct competitors. (By yourself: clearly define the chosen campaign and competitors in your own words.) Analyze the appeals used and infer the advertisement objectives. (By yourself: explain the objectives and justify your interpretation.) Examine the media vehicles used and their scheduling. Report the viewership/readership/listenership of the media, if data is available. Identify and justify the likely target market(s). (By yourself: provide your own reasoning and explanation for the target market analysis.) Evaluate how the media choices support the communication objectives. (By yourself: write your critical evaluation and final conclusion.)
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: This assignment assesses students’ ability to apply media planning knowledge and theories to real-world campaigns. It develops skills in analyzing media strategies, evaluating target markets, and assessing the effectiveness of communication objectives. Students are also expected to demonstrate critical thinking, academic writing, and responsible use of AI tools to support research and analysis.
assessments.Grading Guide: At-home assignment Rubric – Campaign Analysis Assignment (100%) - Understanding of Campaign Context (10%): Identify the role and functions of media planning within marketing, advertising, and communication environments. - Application of Media Psychology & Communication Theories (20%): Evaluate competitive, cultural, and ethical challenges faced by media planners in a dynamic communication environment. - Media Analysis (15%): Analyze media costs, scheduling, and audience measurement to design effective media strategies. - Target Market Justification (10%): Evaluate audience measurement to inform strategy design. - AI Application (15%): Apply tools, software, and artificial intelligence to analyze media data and optimize planning decisions. - Critical Evaluation & Conclusion (10%): Develop professional-standard media plans that integrate diverse media channels and audience insights. - Organization & Writing Quality – Structure, Coherence, Citations (10%): Professional-standard media plan writing and structure. - Grammar & Spelling (10%)
assessments.Note: Based on the predetermined learning outcomes (LOs), lecturers may select appropriate forms of assessment at their discretion.

assessments.Question Type: Each group (maximum 4 students) will create and execute a media project based on the needs of a business or organization. The project will result in both a written report and an oral presentation. Tasks: Analyze the strategic marketing task involved. (By yourself: explain the strategic context and objectives in your own words.) Identify the likely target market(s)/segments. (By yourself: justify the choice of target audience.) Select media channels that match the media usage of the target market(s). Propose a range of target media to purchase, with justification. Develop a detailed media schedule with rationale for each channel/vehicle. Create a bar chart or table illustrating the media scheduling plan. Propose measures for determining campaign success and identify likely failure scenarios with remedial options. (By yourself: provide critical reflections and conclusions.) Prepare a written report (1,500–2,000 words) and visual aids to deliver an oral presentation (10–15 minutes) in class. (By yourself: each member must present in their own words, without AI-generated speech.)
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: This project is a comprehensive test of theoretical knowledge, practical application, creativity, collaboration, and real-world execution — all central to mastering media planning in a professional context. Students are encouraged to use AI tools to support the development and execution of the project.
assessments.Grading Guide: Presentation and Written Report Rubric – Final Project (Total 100%) 1. Written Report (50%) – scored on a 10-point scale Understanding of Strategic Context (10%): Clear explanation of marketing/communication task. (By yourself) Target Market Analysis (10%): Accurate and justified identification of audience segments. (By yourself) Media Plan & Scheduling (20%): Well-structured plan, justified media choices, scheduling chart. AI Application (15%): Effective and ethical use of AI-supported tools; explanation of usefulness and limitations. Critical Reflection & Conclusions (25%): Insightful evaluation of campaign success measures, risks, and remedies. (By yourself) Writing Quality & Organization (20%): Clear structure, academic style, correct citations. Total: 100% of Report = 50% of course grade 2. Oral Presentation (50%) – scored on a 10-point scale Clarity of Presentation (15%): Clear, confident delivery with logical flow. (By yourself) Application of Theories & Concepts (20%): Accurate connection to media planning frameworks. Teamwork & Equal Participation (20%): All members contribute meaningfully. (By yourself) AI Application (15%): Transparent explanation of how AI was used to support the project. Critical Thinking (10%): Demonstrates depth of reasoning and ability to connect insights. (By yourself) Q&A (10%): Thoughtful, direct, and confident responses to lecturer/class questions. (By yourself) Visual Aids & Professionalism (10%): Effective use of slides/visuals, professional appearance. Total: 100% of Presentation = 50% of course grade Option 2 (for Constructivist Approach only): Alternative assessment as proposed by the lecturer

assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions
